newsitem.title: FRANCE: BoF's Trichet backs French govt economic policy.
newsitem.headline: BoF's Trichet backs French govt economic policy.

text.p: Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet on Monday backed the government's drive to cut spending and public deficits and said that it was thanks to this policy that there were lower interest rates in France today.

"We know the direction taken is a good one and, moreover, it was welcomed by investors in France, Europe and the world. And it's thanks to this budget stance, which is clear, 'Maastricht or not Maastricht', that we have interest rates which are clearly very low," Trichet told RTL radio.

"The two worthy points for us are the reduction of spending and the deficit, so there is room for productive investment, ...and in a way that we can have lower market interest rates, which is the case," Trichet said.
Trichet highlighted recent forecasts from the national statistics institute INSEE as showing signs of "a quite strong pick-up" in the economy.
INSEE predicted that there would be an average increase in consumption of about 2.5 percent this year and GDP growth in the third quarter of about one percent versus the preceding one.
The consensus was for growth next year of about 2.3 or 2.4 percent, he said, noting that the Bank itself did not forecast.
"Teams which win are teams with high morale. In Atlanta (Olympic Games) we had the morale and we won. France's economic athletes are every bit as good as the athletes of Atlanta," Trichet said.
Trichet said greater confidence would clearly help but added: "the economy is taking off...the latest data is relatively encouraging.
